THE SIGNALS
 

Four Fort Lauderdale decisions today: $2.9M in CRA money and the Shader site plan

At 1 p.m., Fort Lauderdale's Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) Board takes up nearly $2.9 million across three items: a $2.5 million Holy Cross incentive, Queen Progress's $193,500 conversion grant and $189,952 in Central City planning money. At 6 p.m., the City Commission votes on the Shader Retail site plan. Both meetings are at the police department on West Broward Boulevard. Here's what each action could move, what stays unresolved, and the record behind it.

02

THE PROOF
 
ADVANCE

Ten permit records trace Zara work at Galleria's empty anchor

2442 E. Sunrise Blvd. · Galleria / East Sunrise Boulevard

Ten Fort Lauderdale permit records filed June 26 through Aug. 11 name the Spanish fast-fashion retailer Zara, owned by Inditex, in landlord-work descriptions for the Galleria's former Neiman Marcus building, empty of permanent retail tenants since the store closed in 2020. The permit process is underway; none had been issued as of Aug. 17, and no public lease announcement surfaced in our checks. Zara's official store locator lists seven Florida locations, four in Miami-Dade and none in Broward.

Permit process underway · no public lease announcement in our checks
WHAT CHANGED

The trail starts June 26 with interior-demolition, electrical and plumbing filings at unit Z17. A sprinkler-demolition filing followed July 15. On Aug. 4, a $556,991 main permit described landlord work to prepare the empty retail space, including selective structural reinforcement; five trade applications followed Aug. 11. The filings cover overlapping work, so their declared values should not be added together. Open the $557K main permit →

WHY IT MATTERS

The locator shows Aventura Mall in Miami-Dade as the nearest listed South Florida location. The long-vacant anchor sits inside the Galleria's mall-wide mixed-use repositioning. Wayfair has separately announced a 2027 store. Neither announcement names Zara. The permits establish what was filed with the city, not what is signed.

WHAT WE DON'T KNOW

Whether a lease is signed; the proposed store size, format or opening timetable. BCPA measures the entire building at 96,748 square feet; that is not a Zara-space figure. As of Aug. 17, Florida Signal found no public Zara, Inditex or Galleria announcement naming this address. We also found no indexed prior report.

104 DEEDS
 
Stated consideration on recorded deeds, not permits or appraisals

Broward Clerk records show 106 Fort Lauderdale deeds recorded Aug. 3–9 with nearly $205 million in stated consideration, the amount reported on the deeds rather than an appraisal. Two deeds, the $59.95 million Sea Club transfer and the $44.8 million three-parcel Holman Honda transfer, carried $104.75 million combined. Commercial Observer and the South Florida Business Journal previously reported the transactions.

The concentration is the story, but not the whole story. The other 104 deeds carried about $100 million. Not every recorded deed is an open-market sale, so this measures filing activity, not a market-price index. Source: Broward County official records.

Deeds recorded Aug. 5 · parcel outlines from Broward County records · © OpenStreetMap contributors · © CARTO

Two WREV deeds recorded Aug. 5 list a combined $7.482 million for adjacent industrial parcels: 1610 S. Dixie Highway at $5.1 million and 1500 S. Dixie Highway at $2.382 million. The buyers, WREV Industrial VI and VII, list Tyler Workman as manager and share a West Palm Beach address. Workman is WREV's founding principal; the firm targets $3 million to $35 million industrial deals.

The pair gives owners, tenants and brokers a defined block to watch for permits, construction notices, lease changes or further purchases. The records do not establish buyer intent or a combined redevelopment plan. Open the block in Google Maps →
